claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 20 and lives at home with me. I just wanted to check if I can still claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I'm asking about your son Alex, who is 20 years old and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 20, I need to ask an important question to determine eligibility:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

(For reference, Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 if they stay in approved education or training, but generally stops when a child turns 20 unless specific circumstances apply.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school a while back and he's just been at home, really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask a few more questions to get a complete picture:

**Is Alex currently working, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment. He's been looking for something, but hasn't found anything yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Just to confirm I have all the necessary information:

**When did Alex turn 20 years old?** 

(This is important because Child Benefit eligibility typically ends when a child turns 20, or earlier if they're not in approved education or training after age 16-19.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 20 a few months ago, back in the summer.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: Under UK Child Benefit rules, Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16. For children aged 16 or over, you can still receive Child Benefit if they're under 20 **and** they stay in approved education or training.

Since Alex:
- Is 20 years old (turned 20 a few months ago)
- Is not currently in approved education or training
- Finished school previously and is not in any training program

He does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. The benefit generally stops when a child turns 20, or even earlier (between ages 16-19) if they're not in approved education or training.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he were to enter approved education or training—the rules would still apply based on his age at that time. However, since he's already 20, he would have aged out of the Child Benefit eligibility even if he enters education or training now.

If you have any other questions or need clarification, please let me know.
